title: Chapter 24: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India

blocks.content: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India is a statutory body tasked with regulating and promoting the insurance and re-insurance industries in India.

items: Malhotra Committee (1993) recommended the creation of an independent regulatory authority for the insurance sector.
IRDAI consists of 10 members: 1 Chairman, 5 full-time members, and 4 part-time members.
Headquarters location: Hyderabad, Telangana (shifted from New Delhi in 2001).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI was set up following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee report of 1994.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act was enacted in 1999, granting IRDAI statutory status in April 2000.
The headquarters of IRDAI was relocated from New Delhi to Hyderabad, Telangana, in 2001.
The authority is a 10-member body comprising a Chairman, five full-time members, and four part-time members appointed by the Government of India.
Its core mandate includes protecting policyholder interests, regulating insurance products, and promoting the growth of insurance and re-insurance markets.
